title: AI for Science expands to foundations and institutions
gist: Anthropic is expanding its AI for Science program (free Claude credits, launched May 2025) from individual researchers to 20 funders, institutions and projects — including the US National Science Foundation, Simons and Sloan foundations, STScI, Wellcome Sanger, EMBL, gnomAD and FlyWire — using grant-makers and data-rich institutes as distribution channels. It highlights agentic lab work such as the Model Hardware Standard with HHMI Janelia for AI agents operating lab instruments and Allen Institute agents compressing months of analysis into hours.

themes.theme: Shift from individual grants to institutional distribution

insights.claim: Anthropic expanded its AI for Science program (launched May 2025, giving free Claude credits to researchers) to 20 named scientific foundations, institutions and research groups, moving from supporting individual scientists to partnering with institutions and funders that can reach many more researchers.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Anthropic is using institutional intermediaries as a distribution channel to embed Claude across research workflows at scale.
insights.quote: We started the AI for Science program in May 2025 with the belief that AI could significantly speed up scientific progress.
insights.locator: We started the AI for Science program

insights.claim: Anthropic says the AI for Science effort has already supported hundreds of projects across biology, medicine, physics, chemistry, climate science and mathematics, alongside a discounted Claude Team plan aimed at scientists.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Scientific research is being treated as a deliberate adoption beachhead, with subsidised pricing to seed habitual use.
insights.locator: We started the AI for Science program

insights.claim: Science funders including the Alfred P. Sloan Foundation, Simons Foundation, Schmidt Sciences, Renaissance Philanthropy's Open Source for Science Fund, the US National Science Foundation and CAS (American Chemical Society) will receive Claude credits and redistribute them to researchers, effectively letting grant-makers choose which projects get Anthropic compute.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Outsourcing selection to established funders gives Anthropic credibility and reach without building its own grant apparatus — and ties funder ecosystems to Claude.

insights.claim: The US National Science Foundation, a $9 billion federal agency that accounts for about 25% of federal support for basic research at US colleges and universities, is among the partners distributing Claude credits.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: A federal-agency partnership signals growing government comfort with a specific frontier-model vendor in publicly funded research — a potential precursor to broader public-sector procurement.

insights.claim: Anthropic frames many partnered projects as producers of public goods — open datasets, open-source software, open standards and shared libraries — positioning its credits as infrastructure subsidy for the wider scientific community rather than one-off grants.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Contributing to shared standards and libraries could entrench Claude-compatible tooling as defaults in science.
insights.quote: Many of these projects will also produce public goods that benefit the wider scientific community: open datasets, open-source software, open standards, and shared libraries.
insights.locator: AI for Science began by supporting individual

insights.claim: Anthropic and HHMI Janelia Research Campus developed the Model Hardware Standard (MHS), a shared specification that lets AI agents safely operate lab instruments; MHS is currently in research preview.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: An open standard for agent-instrument control is an early move toward autonomous/self-driving labs, with standard-setters gaining ecosystem leverage — watch lab-instrument makers for adoption.
insights.quote: a shared specification that lets AI agents safely operate lab instruments
insights.locator: For instance, we partnered with HHMI

insights.claim: The Allen Institute is building teams of AI agents to analyze its large open brain, cell and immune-system datasets, which Anthropic says turns months of manual analysis into hours.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Order-of-magnitude compression of analysis time implies labor-cost and cycle-time deflation in data-heavy research.
insights.quote: turning months of manual analysis into hours
insights.locator: We also support the Allen Institute

insights.claim: Scientists report using Claude across the full research loop — generating hypotheses, designing experiments, analyzing complex data and communicating findings — not just for writing assistance.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Usage spanning ideation to analysis suggests deeper workflow lock-in and higher per-seat value in research settings.
insights.quote: Scientists have told us that they’re working with Claude to generate hypotheses, design experiments, swiftly analyze complex data, and communicate findings.
insights.locator: Scientists have told us that they’re

insights.claim: Institutional partners using Claude credits internally include the Space Telescope Science Institute (operations for Hubble, James Webb and Roman telescopes and one of the largest astronomy data archives), Wellcome Sanger Institute, the Francis Crick Institute, Imperial College London's Department of Life Sciences, EMBL and Gladstone Institutes.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: The partner list skews toward owners of large proprietary or reference datasets, where AI agents have the most leverage — and a heavy European life-sciences presence.

insights.claim: EMBL's European Bioinformatics Institute hosts key open data resources biologists use daily, such as Ensembl, Protein Data Bank in Europe and Europe PMC, making it a strategic access point to core biological reference data.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: AI tooling integrated at reference-data hubs could shape how a large share of biologists interact with data.
insights.locator: EMBL. The European Molecular Biology Laboratory

insights.claim: Directly funded new projects include FlyWire (Princeton; first complete wiring map of an adult fruit fly brain), LEAP (Columbia; NSF center combining ML with physics for climate models), AstroPath (Johns Hopkins; astronomy calibration methods to image tumors cell by cell), gnomAD (Broad Institute), Tau Ceti (mathematics) and the Centre for Population Genomics (Australia).
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: The portfolio spans neuroscience, climate, oncology, genomics and math, emphasizing cross-disciplinary, data-intensive problems where AI analysis is the bottleneck.

insights.claim: gnomAD at the Broad Institute pools DNA data from over 800,000 people into an open reference of human genetic variation used by researchers and clinical labs worldwide for rare disease diagnosis.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: AI applied to population-scale genomic references could accelerate rare-disease diagnostics, a clinical-genomics growth area.
insights.quote: pools DNA data from over 800,000 people into an open reference of human genetic variation

insights.claim: Tau Ceti is an open, community-driven project building a shared autoformalized library of mathematics in Lean, where computers check every proof — a target where AI output is machine-verifiable.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Formal verification gives an objective correctness check on AI-generated reasoning, a key ingredient for trustworthy AI in math and beyond.
insights.quote: building a shared autoformalized library of mathematics in Lean, a language that lets computers check every proof

insights.claim: Anthropic acknowledges many of these collaborations are still in early stages, with impact yet to be demonstrated, and says it hopes to expand to more partners globally.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Treat the announcement as go-to-market and positioning rather than evidence of scientific breakthroughs; measurable results are still pending.
insights.quote: Many of these collaborations are still in their early stages
